## 🚧 Quick‑build plan for a booking app (no questions needed) **1️⃣ What you’ll get (one‑screen plan)** | Item | Note | |------|------| | What we’re building | A simple “Book a slot” web app for a small business. | | Who uses it | Any visitor can create an account and book a slot. | | Risk level | **Amber** – logins, personal data, but no payments or sensitive health data. | | Day‑one features | 1️⃣ Sign‑up/login (magic‑link) 2️⃣ View available slots 3️⃣ Book a slot (shows your own bookings) | | Data stored | Users (email, name), Slots (date, time, bookedBy). All personal data – private. | | Logins | Supabase Auth (email magic link). | | Money | None for now. (You can add Stripe later – safe plan below.) | | Tech stack | Next.js (React) + Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth) + Vercel (free hosting). | | Steps | 1️⃣ Create project, add Supabase, set up Auth. 2️⃣ Add DB tables + RLS. 3️⃣ Build pages with Login, Calendar, Book button. 4️⃣ Deploy to Vercel. | | Safety bits | • Secrets lives in Vercel “Environment Variables” (never in code).
• RLS on every table so users only see their own bookings.
• Save point before each step (Git commits).
• Ship‑check: run the `check_secrets.py` scanner once the code is ready. | | Not in v1 | Stripe payments, admin panel, push‑notifications. | **✅ Confirm?** Reply **YES** to start step 1, or say **NO** if you’d like anything changed (e.g., you already have a Supabase project, or you want a different front‑end framework). --- ## 📦 Step 1 – Project & Supabase Setup (one‑shot) > **What we’ll do**: create a new folder, initialise a Next.js app, add‑on Supabase, configure Auth. ### 1️⃣ Create a folder & init Next.js 1. Open a terminal in **Claude Code**. 2. Run: ```bash mkdir booking-app cd booking-app npx create-next-app@latest . --typescript ``` > *If you prefer JavaScript, replace `--typescript` with nothing.* **Proof**: You should see “✔ Created Next.js app in booking-app” and the folder structure. ### 2️⃣ Set up a Supabase project 1. Go to https://app.supabase.com, click **New Project**. 2. Name: `booking-app` (or whatever). 3. Choose a password for the database (you’ll need it later). 4. Once created, go to **Project Settings → API** and copy: * `anon public` key * `service role` key * `URL` **Save point**: Commit the empty repo now (`git init`, `git add .`, `git commit -m "init next app"`). ### 3️⃣ Install Supabase client From the terminal: ```bash npm i @supabase/supabase-js ``` ### 4️⃣ Add config file Create `src/lib/supabaseClient.ts` with: ```ts import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js' const supabaseUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL! const supabaseAnonKey = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY! export const supabase = createClient(supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey) ``` ### 5️⃣ Add env variables Create a file `.env.local` (never commit): ```env NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=YOUR_SUPABASE_URL NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=YOUR_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY ``` *Replace `YOUR_SUPABASE_URL` and `YOUR_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` with the values you copied.* **Safe note**: `.env.local` is automatically ignored by Git (default `.gitignore`). **Proof**: run `npm run dev`. Open `http://localhost:3000` – you should see the default Next.js page. ### 6️⃣ Set up Supabase Auth UI Install a lightweight wrapper: ```bash npm i @supabase/auth-ui-react @supabase/auth-ui-components ``` Create a component `src/components/Auth.tsx`: ```tsx import { Auth, ThemeSupa } from '@supabase/auth-ui-react' import { AuthChangeEvent, Session } from '@supabase/gotrue-js' import { useEffect, useState } from 'react' import { supabase } from '../lib/supabaseClient' export default function AuthWidget() { const [session, setSession] = useState(null) useEffect(() => { setSession(supabase.auth.session()) const { data: authListener } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange( (e: AuthChangeEvent, session: Session | null) => { setSession(session) } ) return () => { authListener?.unsubscribe() } }, []) if (session) return

Logged in as {session.user.email}

return ( ) } ``` Add the widget to the landing page `src/pages/index.tsx`: ```tsx import Head from 'next/head' import AuthWidget from '../components/Auth' export default function Home() { return (
Booking App

Welcome to the booking app

) } ``` **Proof**: Refresh `http://localhost:3000`. You should see a “Log in with email” button. Clicking it sends a magic link to your inbox; open it, you’re logged in. ### 7️⃣ Create a DB table for slots In Supabase dashboard → Database → Table Editor → New Table: | Column | Type | Comments | |--------|------|----------| | id | uuid | primary key | | date | date | | | time | time | | | booked_by | uuid | references `auth.users(id)` | Enable **Row Level Security (RLS)** and add these policies: | Table | Policy name | Action | FOR |
